title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Horizon Bank
summary: Weekly POC security sync between Redwood and Horizon Bank. Main items: SSO testing (SAML), audit log access and retention, SOC2 evidence and gaps, KMS integration questions, and next steps for pilot completion. Redwood AE + SE to share docs and schedule a network/infra deep dive.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated SAML config guide and a test IdP account details (by 2026-10-16)
Customer to provide sample audit logs and current retention policy (by 2026-10-20)
Run full E2E SSO test with Horizon QA by 2026-10-21
Schedule infra/networking deep-dive (on-site or VPN) week of 2026-10-26
action_items: John Miller - Provide SAML metadata + test IdP account (Due: 2026-10-21)
Priya Rao - Share SOC2 report summary, security checklist, and pilot benchmark sheet (Due: 2026-10-16)
Aisha Khan - Send current log retention policy and SIEM ingestion details (Due: 2026-10-20)
Alex Nguyen - Arrange infra deep-dive and share VPN/port requirements doc (Due: 2026-10-18)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), John Miller (CISO, Horizon Bank), Aisha Khan (Head of Cloud), Marco Ruiz (DevOps)
Shared: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf, shared drive: /horizon/pilot/benchmarks.xlsx

[00:00] Alex Nguyen: hey everyone, thanks for joining for the weekly pilot security sync, we'll run through SSO, logs and SOC2 items, quick roll call?
[00:18] John Miller: john here, yep, aisha, marco on too
[00:22] Aisha Khan: hi all, aisha here
[00:25] Marco Ruiz: marco - hey
[00:30] Priya Rao: priya from redwood, se on the pilot, i'll take the technical bits on the saml and logs
[01:05] Alex Nguyen: quick agenda - 1) SSO status 2) Audit logs + retention 3) SOC2 evidence questions 4) KMS/encryption + network touch points 5) next steps
[01:28] John Miller: for SSO we tried the metadata you sent last week, we saw an error about audience uri mismatch, so we've blocked testing until we align on the sp-entity id and the cert thumbprint
[01:45] Priya Rao: ok yeah that sounds like the audience/acs mismatch; in our last send i think the SP entity was redwood-inferenc-prod, but maybe you have a different naming convention - sorry sometimes our export says "redwood-dedicate" in the metadata which causes confusion
[02:10] Marco Ruiz: also note our IdP rotates certs nightly in staging - that's for testing, but we can produce a stable test cert if needed
[02:28] Priya Rao: that would help, also we can provide a test IdP account and a stripped down metadata file. i'll attach the step-by-step saml guide after this call (see action items).
[03:00] John Miller: perfect, we also need to confirm SSO session timeout mapping to our RBAC sessions - can your platform accept assertion lifetime mapping?
[03:18] Priya Rao: yes we map session TTLs to the IdP assertion but there are limits on long running streaming sessions for chat. we'll document typical behaviors and knobs. sometimes the transcript from our test says "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" in our logs, sorry the speech-to-text in the recording had funny substitutions earlier, but i mean KV cache for token caching
[03:50] Alex Nguyen: moving on to audit logging - horizon asked for both admin/audit logs and token-level usage logs. john, can you remind us what your SIEM expects?
[04:05] John Miller: we push to Splunk. primary needs: auth events (login, SAML success/fail), admin actions (config changes), and per-request metadata for a sample of the calls - we don't need full payloads but we want request ids, timestamp, model id and route, and redacted prompt hashes for correlation
[04:35] Priya Rao: got it. Redwood's hosted API emits structured events and we can stream to an HTTP endpoint or s3 bucket. during pilot we can provide a sample feed to your SIEM. small note - our current pilot retention in hosted mode is 30 days by default but we can configure retention for dedicated/private deployments
[05:05] Aisha Khan: 30 days is our baseline too but we may need 7-year retention for some records for compliance - that's for backups/archival not hot logs. are you able to push cold archives to our s3 in the right region?
[05:23] Priya Rao: yes for dedicated/private we support archiving to customer-owned S3 buckets with lifecycle rules; for hosted we can pull-request archives but we need legal ok. we'll capture the exact flow in the doc.
[05:45] Marco Ruiz: what about encryption keys? we need BYOK and HSM support for production - SOC requirements list that explicitly
[05:55] Priya Rao: Redwood supports KMS integrations; for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and we have options for customer-managed keys. for hosted we offer an envelope encryption model using CMKs in partner KMSs - i will share the KMS integration guide
[06:20] John Miller: and audit trails for key usage? we need to see key use logs for crypto ops
[06:30] Priya Rao: yes, key usage logs come from your KMS; we can correlate operation ids to our request ids if you share the KMS audit events - some mapping work required but doable as part of pilot
[06:50] Alex Nguyen: SOC 2 - john, you sent a list of evidence items last week; priya, can you speak to what we can provide during pilot vs what requires dedicated deployment?
[07:05] Priya Rao: during pilot we can provide the majority of operational evidence: access logs, config change logs, incident response playbook, and architecture diagrams. full SOC2 audited artifacts (i.e., the formal SOC2 report for the service) is available but for dedicated/private we can provide a scoped report and contractual assurances. i'll flag that sometimes the SOC2 PDF contains redacted sections - i'll send the summary and point you to the SOC2 binder link we shared earlier
[07:40] John Miller: right we want to see attestations for encryption, RBAC, and change management. also need to know which controls are covered in hosted vs dedicated
[07:55] Priya Rao: we'll produce a control-matrix mapping showing hosted/dedicated/private and which controls are in scope; that'll be part of the SOC2 evidence pack Priya to send (action item)
[08:15] Marco Ruiz: networking - we had an issue yesterday where outbound ports to your cluster were blocked, we need a clear list of IPs and ports for the pilot. can you provide an IP range?
[08:28] Alex Nguyen: yes, we'll share the ip ranges (note: for hosted these are dynamic so we recommend private link or VPN; for dedicated we'll give deterministic ranges). i'll add a VPN/ports doc to the drive
[09:00] John Miller: ok on the pilot results - we ran the sample 1k request test last week, latency median looks ok but p95 spiked when batching happened - can you explain tradeoffs again?
[09:18] Priya Rao: sure, batching reduces cost but can increase p95 latency due to queueing. for the pilot we used default batching config; we can tune batch size and batching window to match your latency SLOs. also KV cache hit rates matter - with more cache hits we see big p95 improvements
[09:45] Marco Ruiz: hitting cache is dependent on prompt prefixing - are you doing prefix caching here?
[09:52] Priya Rao: yes we do prefix/KV caching but it depends on identical prefixes across calls; we'll provide guidance on how to structure prompts and route calls to improve hit rates. sometimes the docs call out "Redwood Console" as "Redwood Consol" in transcripts, ignore small typos in the recording
[10:20] Alex Nguyen: back to compliance - john asked about data residency. horizon told us they need logs stored in us-east-1 for this pilot and europe for other regions; can you confirm?
[10:34] John Miller: yes us-east for pilot, but production will be multi-region - europe and apac later next year
[10:40] Priya Rao: we can pin storage to a region for logs and archival for dedicated/private. for hosted we'll need a contract addendum for region-specific retention; as noted earlier we can push archives to your S3 in selected regions
[11:05] Aisha Khan: a small sec question - who has access to plaintext prompts in Redwood's hosted logs? we need minimal exposure; ideally only metadata + hashes
[11:18] Priya Rao: in hosted mode by default we log metadata and a redacted prompt hash and we do not persist full plaintext prompts unless you opt-in for debugging. Dedicated/private can be configured to never persist plaintext to Redwood storage, instead write to your storage. we will document exact fields emitted to logs in the log schema doc
[11:45] John Miller: good. also need retention SLA for logs if there's a subpoena or legal hold - can you do legal hold on archived buckets?
[11:55] Alex Nguyen: yes if archives are in customer-owned buckets you control legal holds; for hosted archives we have a process to freeze data but we need legal approval - i'll note that as a follow-up
[12:20] Priya Rao: quick note: during previous calls some of our transcriptions mis-typed product names so if you see "redwood inferce" that was the ASR - ignore it
[12:40] Marco Ruiz: security scanning - we need to run a vulnerability scan against the connector during integration windows, is there a process?
[12:50] Priya Rao: yes we have a security onboarding doc and can coordinate an approved scan window with our security team. for private deployments you can run full network scans; for hosted we require a signed NDA and limited scanning scope. i'll add the security onboarding link
[13:18] John Miller: on SLA: if we move to dedicated for production we need 99.95% uptime and incident response times - do you offer that?
[13:30] Alex Nguyen: yes Dedicated comes with an SLA and a named technical contact and faster incident response. we'll share the SLA doc and the escalation matrix
[13:50] Aisha Khan: a short question on logging format - can you output JSON events with a stable schema so our Logstash parsers can handle them?
[13:58] Priya Rao: yes structured JSON events, we'll include a sample schema in the log doc (fields: timestamp, request_id, model, route, user_id_hash, action).
[14:25] John Miller: looking at risk items - the team flagged SOC2 control CC-6 for encryption at rest, can you confirm coverage?
[14:38] Priya Rao: CC-6 is covered for dedicated/private; for hosted we have encryption at rest with provider-managed keys and envelope encryption; the control-matrix will call out the exact mapping and any compensating controls
[15:05] Alex Nguyen: ok want to recap next steps?
[15:12] John Miller: yes and then we'll aim to run the SSO test next week
[15:20] Alex Nguyen: recap: Redwood sends SAML guide + test IdP, SOC2 summary + control matrix, KMS integration guide, log schema and port/ip ranges. Horizon to provide SAML metadata, sample logs, retention policy, and run E2E test. schedule infra deep-dive for week of 10/26.
[15:45] Priya Rao: i'll send the docs after the call - SOC2 summary link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2-summary.pdf and SAML guide: https://redwood.ai/docs/saml-setup.pdf
[16:05] John Miller: thanks, that helps. any blockers?
[16:10] Marco Ruiz: no blockers besides cert stability for IdP, we'll provide a stable cert for testing
[16:20] Alex Nguyen: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the doc bundle and action items noted.
[16:30] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (product names, "KV cash" mis-hearing). Links above are shared artifacts for the pilot (security binder, saml guide, benchmark sheet).
